item.title: A New Degree of Freedom in Stellarator Coil Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.14396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reversed toroidal field (RTF) coils introduce a new degree of freedom in stellarator coil design. While the total plasma-linked current is fixed by Ampere's law, compensating RTF currents allow the modular-coil current to exceed this value without altering the net linkage. This redistribution decouples key coil constraints and modifies the external coil geometry without significantly compromising the confining magnetic field. As a result, the achievable coil-plasma separation can be increased in the configurations studied, potentially enabling more compact stellarator designs.
item.dc:creator: Sophia A. Henneberg, Annika Zettl

item.title: SPIRE: Spin-Resolved Particle-in-Cell with Radiative Corrections for Extreme Laser--Plasma Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present SPIRE, a spin- and photon-polarization-resolved particle-in-cell (PIC) code for self-consistent simulations of laser-plasma interactions in the strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED) regime. The classical PIC framework combines a Yee-grid finite-difference time-domain Maxwell solver, a relativistic Boris particle pusher, shape-function particle-grid interpolation, Esirkepov charge-conserving current deposition, laser boundary injection, and a relativistic moving window in one, two, and three spatial dimensions. A vectorial Laguerre-Gaussian laser injector based on an angular-spectrum formulation supports tightly focused, nonparaxial optical orbital-angular-momentum modes. The strong-field QED module treats nonlinear Compton scattering and nonlinear Breit-Wheeler pair production as stochastic processes using spin- and polarization-resolved probabilities in the local constant-field approximation. Electron and positron spin evolution includes stochastic transitions, no-emission corrections, and Thomas-Bargmann-Michel-Telegdi precession with a field-dependent anomalous magnetic moment. Photon polarization is represented by the Stokes vector and evolves through nonlinear Compton scattering, pair production, vacuum birefringence, and vacuum dichroism. The implementation is verified with one-, two-, and three-dimensional benchmarks. Classical PIC results are cross-checked against SMILEI, and the spin- and polarization-resolved QED modules reproduce published results for polarized electron generation, vacuum birefringence and dichroism, and dense polarized positron production. These benchmarks verify the coupled classical PIC, strong-field QED, spin, and photon-polarization modules implemented in SPIRE.
item.dc:creator: Xian-Zhang Wu, Huai-Hang Song, Wei-Min Wang, Yan-Fei Li

item.title: First achievement of 100 million degree electron temperatures in a spherical torus: the EXL-50U
item.description: arXiv:2610.14684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Here,we report an ST plasma in which Thomson scattering measures a central electron temperature exceeding 8.6 keV (100 million degrees kelvin) on the EXL-50U spherical torus device.The high-temperature phase is obtained at low density by sequential operation of two 50 GHz ECRH systems: ordinary-mode (O-mode) ECRH3 followed by extraordinary-mode (X-mode) ECRH4. In contrast to neutral-beam-heated high-ion-temperature ST scenarios, the discharge is sustained by ECRH only.
item.dc:creator: Guang Yang, Shaodong Song, Songjian Li, Xiaobing Xie, Zhaokun Wang, Xiang Gu, Jia Li, Xianli Huang, Xinchen Jiang, Yupeng Guan, Huicong Ma, Junquan Lin, Dong Guo, Jiaqi Dong, Yunfeng Liang, Yuejiang Shi, the EXL-50U Team

item.title: Plasma-neutral collision operators for hydrogen isotopes: kinetic and gyrokinetic descriptions, comparison to fluid
item.description: arXiv:2610.15090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Plasma-neutral interactions critically affect the edge dynamics of magnetically confined fusion devices. Neutral atoms modify ion and electron velocity distributions, potentially affecting local instabilities Standard fluid models simplify these processes (namely charge exchange, ionization and recombination) using Maxwellian assumptions and linearized source terms. We revisit these assumptions for a hydrogen plasma interacting with hydrogen atoms. We derive plasma-neutral interaction terms in the kinetic and gyrokinetic frameworks. Accounting for velocity-dependent differential cross-sections, the model captures the kinetic impact of inelastic collisions on ions and electrons beyond energy and momentum exchange. We demonstrate that the fluid moments of the kinetic model reduce to standard fluid source terms under the appropriate assumptions of Maxwellianity and linearity. We compare the kinetic model with fluid models through their effects on distribution functions and fluid moments. Substantial discrepancies are observed, even for Maxwellian distributions. For charge exchange, the kinetic model yields momentum and energy exchange rates up to twice those predicted by fluid descriptions. We show that a fluid treatment of ionization greatly overestimates the mean kinetic energy of the produced electrons. These results highlight the limitations of fluid descriptions and the importance of kinetic effects in edge-plasma momentum and energy exchange.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Protais, Guilhem Dif-Pradalier, Yanick Sarazin, Virginie Grandgirard, Yannick Marandet, Srikanth Sureshkumar, Naren Varadarajan

item.title: A reduced model for neoclassical transport in non-axisymmetric magnetic configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A unified framework is proposed to compute a neoclassical equilibrium for tokamaks with non-axisymmetric magnetic perturbations, based on a Hamiltonian description combined with a variational approach that relies on a principle of minimum entropy production. This approach allows for a transparent identification of the respective contributions from different classes of trapped particles in magnetic well minima. Analytic expressions are derived for specific collisionality regimes, and a fast and efficient numerical procedure is devised to compute the entropy production rate. Finding the extremum of the entropy production leads to tractable expressions of transport coefficients that can be computed quickly and efficiently.
item.dc:creator: Y. Ban, X. Garbet, R. Varennes, Z. Qu, K. Lim, Y. Sarazin, A. Ibrahim, Y. C. Tay, B. B. Ang

item.title: Implicit PIC Simulations of Hydrogen Plasmas with Intense Negative Ion Production
item.description: arXiv:2610.16257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-density plasma discharges in hydrogen operating at low pressures are of considerable interest for negative ion production used in many applications. Their weak collisionality requires a kinetic, nonlocal description, and a popular approach is to model such discharges numerically using the particle-in-cell (PIC) method combined with Monte Carlo collisions (MCC). However, the most commonly used explicit momentumconserving variant of this method is highly inefficient because it must resolve both the Debye length and the plasma period. In this context, the implicit energy-conserving PIC/MCC scheme appears to be an attractive alternative, as it can model the plasmas of interest using their actual parameters without resorting to artificial scaling techniques. This work considers simulations of two types of high-density plasma discharges performed using electromagnetic or electrostatic energy-conserving PIC/MCC codes in hydrogen, and discusses the observed negative ion production.
item.dc:creator: Denis Eremin

item.title: Relativistic Six-Fluid Rotating-Plasma Force-Balance Equilibria for p-11B Fusion Conditions in Spherical Tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.16304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate an axisymmetric spherical torus (ST) six-component magnetofluid equilibrium model for p_11B plasmas composed of thermal and suprathermal proton, boron, and electron fluids. The model is designed for p_11B parameter regimes where ion energies, strong current drive, energetic electron populations, and ion-electron temperature separation can render a single_fluid static_equilibrium description inadequate. It generalizes rotating_plasma equilibrium theory by incorporating relativistic thermal enthalpy corrections to the electron fluids via h(T/m_ec^2) and by constructing modified flux functions Y_{\alpha} associated with canonical angular momentum for each component {\alpha}. The equilibrium is determined by a Grad-Shafranov-like Ampere law for the poloidal magnetic flux Psi, algebraic density relations constrained by quasineutrality, and prescribed profile functions F_{\alpha}(Y_{\alpha}), T_{\alpha}(Y_{\alpha}) and K_{\alpha}(Y_{\alpha}). The manuscript includes the relativistic magnetofluid equations, the axisymmetric equilibrium formulation, the six_fluid computational method, and four numerical equilibria: two reactor_relevant ST p_11B parameter sets and two EHL-2 ST cases. The examples span toroidal beta b_T = 0.058_0.253, plasma currents I_p = 2.697_12.59 MA, and suprathermal electron temperatures T_eh = 287 keV_2.37 MeV, with h up to 19.1. Over these parameter ranges, Ampere's law accuracy, electrostatic potential accuracy, and component_resolved radial force balance can have errors ranging from 3% to below 0.1%. These results indicate that high-temperature p_11B ST equilibria can differ qualitatively from the single_fluid tokamak equilibria and require analysis of equilibrium component_resolved force balance, relativistic electron enthalpy, and explicit reproducibility diagnostics.
item.dc:creator: Yueng_Kay Martin Peng, Akio Ishida

item.title: QUARZ: a quasi-static particle-in-cell code with non-uniform radial grids for plasma wakefields
item.description: arXiv:2610.16910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a quasi-static particle-in-cell scheme for beam-driven plasma wakefields in cylindrical geometry that works on an arbitrary non-uniform radial grid. The field equations are discretized with hat-function finite elements and conservative finite volumes on any monotone set of radial nodes, and the transverse magnetic field is obtained explicitly, without iterations, following Baxevanis and Stupakov. An optional azimuthal mode $m=1$ describes beam offsets, tilts and hosing. The discretization keeps the discrete Gauss law exact, deposits a uniform plasma exactly on every node including the axis, and remains second-order accurate on smoothly stretched grids. Resolution can therefore be placed where the physics needs it. For a tightly focused witness beam that pulls the plasma ions onto the axis, a grid that is fine only near the axis gives the same near-axis fields as a uniform grid with the same axis resolution, with thirty times fewer cells and in thirty times less computing time. Such a grid also resolves the singular closure of a cold-plasma bubble, which a uniform grid hides by smoothing it over one cell; smoothing the plasma sources over a fixed length, chosen independently of the grid, regularizes the closure and makes the wake behind it converge. The scheme is implemented in the open-source C++/Kokkos code QUARZ (Quasistatic Arbitrary-resolution RZ), which runs on CPUs and GPUs and uses MPI with a pipelined decomposition along the co-moving coordinate. Simulations of the self-modulation of the AWAKE proton bunch agree with the three-dimensional code HiPACE++. QUARZ is, to our knowledge, the first production-grade simulation code in plasma physics that is \emph{zero-touch}: all of its source code, tests and documentation were written by an AI agent directed by a physicist who did not write a single line of the code.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Pukhov, Thomas C. Wilson

item.title: Dynamic Optimization Workflow for Gyrokinetic Stability and Transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.17496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A dynamic optimization workflow for linear gyrokinetic stability that couples the gyrokinetic code CGYRO with the libEnsemble framework for ensemble management has been developed. The workflow is designed to efficiently explore multi-dimensional plasma parameter spaces and to address the practical challenges of simulation-driven optimization in fusion plasma physics, including expensive objective evaluations, unavailable gradient information, non-smoothness arising from transitions between dominant instability branches, and simultaneous multi-core simulations on high-performance computing resources. Rather than optimizing the growth rate at a single wavenumber, the objective maximizes the growth rate-to-wavenumber ratio over the ion-scale spectrum. A derivative-free, model-based optimization algorithm employs manifold sampling to handle the nonsmooth composite structure of the objective function. The approach is applied to the optimization of local magnetic flux-surface shaping parameters, with an equilibrium baseline drawn from DIII-D negative triangularity experimental parameters. The workflow is general and extensible and provides a foundation for future optimization studies involving nonlinear transport objectives and higher-dimensional parameter spaces.
item.dc:creator: E. A. Belli, J. Larson, J. Candy, I. Sfiligoi

item.title: Effects of Coulomb Collisions on the Structures of Fast Magnetosonic Shocks
item.description: arXiv:2610.17594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations to demonstrate qualitative effects of binary Coulomb collisions on fast magnetosonic shocks. We find that with sufficiently high collisional frequencies, shock rippling and reformation can be inhibited, leading to stationary, laminar shock fronts. We observe that ion-ion collisions disrupt the motion of particles reflected back upstream that is the key for cyclical reformation. Meanwhile, the electron-ion collisions provide a Spitzer resistivity that can dissipate energy from the instability that causes shock rippling. This result helps us understand the role of collisions in laboratory shocks and possibly the outer heliosphere.
item.dc:creator: Michael B. Farnell III, Fan Guo, Yi-Hsin Liu, Xiaocan Li

item.title: Validation of geometric proxies using negative and positive triangularity plasmas with varying elongation on TCV and multi-machine gyrokinetic simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Negative Triangularity (NT) tokamak plasmas can achieve H-mode-like confinement while avoiding Edge Localized Modes, making them an attractive reactor scenario. Predicting in which configuration this benefit occurs requires understanding how magnetic geometry controls turbulent transport. Using a set of geometric proxies based on the poloidally averaged magnetic drift velocity, its poloidal variation, and Finite Larmor Radius (FLR) effects, this work validates their predictive power against gyrokinetic simulations and experiments. First, the proxies are used to predict how the relative benefit of NT over Positive Triangularity (PT) evolves with elongation $\kappa$, forecasting a detrimental effect of NT below $\kappa\sim0.75$--$0.8$. This prediction is confirmed by linear and nonlinear GENE simulations in both ITG- and TEM-dominated regimes. Additionally, a dedicated experimental elongation scan on TCV shows that NT plasmas at $\kappa^{\rm LCFS}=1.5$ have $\beta_N$ and $H_{98y2}$ roughly 1.5 times larger than PT counterparts, while no difference is observed at $\kappa^{\rm LCFS}=0.95$. The analysis is then extended to realistic ITG-dominated scenarios from DIII-D, AUG, and JET, including up-down asymmetric equilibria where conventional triangularity-based descriptions break down. In all three devices, simulations of NT equilibria exhibit substantially reduced nonlinear heat fluxes relative to PT (factors of 1.8, 1.6, and 2.1, respectively). A systematic swap of geometric coefficients between NT and PT equilibria shows that magnetic drifts and FLR effects are the dominant stabilizing mechanisms across all machines, with parallel dynamics playing a secondary role. These results establish the geometric proxies as reliable, computationally inexpensive predictors of NT transport benefits across diverse shapes and turbulence regimes.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Balestri, Justin Ball, Stefano Coda, Olivier Sauter, Paola Mantica, Alberto Mariani, Benoit Labit, Branka Vanovac, Joerg Hobirk, the TCV team

item.title: Controlling writhe in stellarator optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.18190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The writhe of a closed curve measures its coiling, and for a ribbon along it, writhe is the contribution to the linking number not due to twist. In stellarators, large writhe implies large helical excursion and has previously been either an uncontrolled outcome in optimization, or fixed beforehand by the choice of the coordinate system. We present a simple method to target the underlying writhe of the plasma boundary during optimization. Our method calculates writhe and linking number directly from the underlying elliptical boundary of the stellarator. It therefore does not require any properties of the MHD equilibrium solve, such as the true magnetic axis, making it fast to evaluate and smooth to differentiate. Examples for quasi-helically symmetric stellarators show that this target works well in practice.
item.dc:creator: Tobias M. Schuett, Sophia A. Henneberg

item.title: Multi-Objective Design of C-Shaped Targets for Energy--Divergence Control in Laser-Driven Proton Acceleration
item.description: arXiv:2610.14824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We optimize the energy-divergence trade-off of laser-driven protons from a C-shaped target using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations and constrained multi-objective Bayesian optimization. Five geometry and focusing parameters are varied to maximize proton cutoff energy and minimize the RMS divergence of forward protons with E_k >= 5 MeV under a proton-only conversion-efficiency constraint of eta_H >= 9%. Of 82 designs, 60 are feasible and 15 Pareto-optimal. The Max-Energy and Min-Divergence endpoints yield 28.64 MeV at 52.51 degrees and 11.47 MeV at 11.13 degrees, respectively; a representative compromise yields 21.44 MeV at 38.44 degrees. Matched-stage diagnostics link these regimes to optical-field buildup, electron energization, charge separation, and outer-sheath organization. Numerical tests support the principal trends. Reflection timing does not support a monotonic trapping-duration law, and the charge-sheath relation remains non-local. These results establish a design-resolved route to controlling proton energy and angular quality.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Rezaei-Pandari, Mahdi Shayganmanesh, Mohammad Hossein Mahdieh

item.title: Toward a Multimodal Foundation Model for Plasma State Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.15076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Plasma experiments observe coupled physical states through sparse, heterogeneous, and incomplete diagnostics. We present a proof of concept toward a multimodal foundation model for plasma state reconstruction during magnetic reconnection, motivated by the Facility for Laboratory Reconnection Experiments (FLARE). Using 250 synthetic VPIC simulations at fixed reference electron beta $\beta_{e0}=0.2$, with 225 training runs and 25 disjoint validation runs, we train a 5.5M-parameter residual 3D U-Net to reconstruct three magnetic-field components and electron density from incomplete observations. The model combines spatial-only pooling, which preserves all 24 temporal frames, with global spatiotemporal self-attention and rotary positional encoding. Independently masking magnetic and density modalities across random, grid, block, and temporal patterns enables sparse sensing, cross-modal completion, density super-resolution, and temporal completion with a single set of weights and no task-specific retraining. With density fully hidden, just 0.1% magnetic spatial visibility reduces median density NRMSE from approximately 0.9 to 0.1. Conversely, observed density improves current-density reconstruction when magnetic data are absent or extremely sparse. With no magnetic observations, roughly 1% density visibility approaches the density reconstruction accuracy achieved with fully observed magnetic fields, although current structure remains more dependent on direct magnetic measurements. Full magnetic conditioning also stabilizes completion of missing future density frames. These results demonstrate bidirectional cross-modal predictive coupling within this simulation regime. Generalization across plasma regimes or to experimental measurements remains untested.
item.dc:creator: Bin Xia, Chuanfei Dong, Boting Li, Yilan Qin, Zikang Xie, Sung Hyun Son, Adam J. Stanier, Jongsoo Yoo, Hantao Ji, Ahmed Diallo, Han Ding, John Wise

item.title: Radial increase of the compensated interplanetary magnetic field magnitude as a result of the growth of spherically polarized Alfv\'en waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Measurements from the NASA Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission demonstrate that inside $\sim20$ solar radii ($\Rs$) the magnitude of the interplanetary magnetic field does not fall off simply as $1/R^2$, with $\avg{|B|}\,R^2$ 15--20\% below its value at $\sim60\,\Rs$. Here we use PSP magnetic field measurements over $10.6$--$56.8\,\Rs$ to show that the outward rise of $\avg{|B|}\,R^2$ is not due to the global structure of the heliospheric magnetic field or proximity to the heliospheric current sheet but is the direct result of the growth of large-amplitude, spherically polarized Alfv\'en waves (so-called `switchbacks'). Over the same distance range, $\avg{B_R}\,R^2$ stays constant, so that the sector-signed radial flux is conserved. The wave amplitude $\epsilon = B_{\perp,{\rm rms}}/\avg{B_\parallel}$ grows from $0.26$ to $0.57$ as $R^{1/2}\cos\alpha$, and $\avg{|B|}/\avg{B_R}$ rises by $20\%$. A simple model parametrized by the broadening of the distribution of deflection angles reproduces the effect to high accuracy. These results demonstrate that as the relative wave amplitudes grow with increasing solar distance, a dynamo-like process operates to enhance the field magnitude by up to $20\%$. By enhancing magnetic pressure this has implications for the large scale solar wind structure in the low-beta inner heliosphere, as well as partially resolving the long-standing discrepancy between remote measurements of the solar magnetic field and those made in situ by earlier missions farther from the Sun.
item.dc:creator: Stuart D. Bale, Timothy S. Horbury, Lorenzo Matteini

item.title: A modern particle-in-cell code for beam-beam simulations of future colliders
item.description: arXiv:2610.17557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A key challenge in the design of next-generation colliders is predicting the effects of beam-beam interactions and using these predictions to optimize machine performance. Beam-beam interactions are characterized by strong focusing forces, radiative effects, and the generation of background particles. While analytical formulas provide insight into the dynamics of beam-beam interactions, these nonlinear, coupled effects are most accurately described with numerical methods. In this paper, we introduce the open-source particle-in-cell code WarpX as a modern tool for modeling the interaction point in future lepton colliders. WarpX provides high-performance execution on distributed GPU architectures within an open-source and actively maintained code base. We present convergence scans and benchmarks against the established beam-beam codes GUINEA-PIG (v1.2.2) and CAIN (v2.42) for luminosity spectra, photon emission, and secondary-particle production under a wide range of beam parameters corresponding to different collider concepts. Our results show that WarpX (v26.09) reproduces the benchmark beam-beam observables while enabling GPU-portable, extensible simulations. These results establish WarpX as a scalable platform for high-fidelity beam-beam modeling in future collider studies.
item.dc:creator: Arianna Formenti, Remi Lehe, Axel Huebl, Stepan S. Bulanov, Jens Osterhoff, Andrew Myers, Weiqun Zhang, Spencer Gessner, Peter Kicsiny, Anna Kinderman, Bao Nguyen, Jinseo Park, Jean-Luc Vay

item.title: A simple procedure for generating a Kappa distribution in PIC simulation
item.description: arXiv:2512.04272v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For kinetic modeling of plasma processes in space, a rejection-sampling procedure for generating a Kappa distribution in particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation is proposed. A Pareto distribution is employed as an envelope distribution. The procedure only requires uniform variates, and its acceptance efficiency is $\approx 0.73$--$0.8$.
item.dc:creator: Seiji Zenitani

item.title: Stellarator island divertor shape optimization for reduced peak heat fluxes
item.description: arXiv:2602.24049v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An automated algorithm to construct island divertors for stellarators is presented and used to find divertors that meet heat load requirements determined by material limits. The algorithm uses just two initial conditions: two starting coordinates on the island separatrix chosen by the user. We leverage the simplicity of the algorithm to explore the divertor parameter space in a fixed magnetic equilibrium. Heat loads are approximated using the field line diffusion model implemented in the \texttt{FLARE} code. Divertor solutions that satisfy heat load requirements while maintaining a high power fraction captured are found using a parameter scan and a Bayesian optimization routine. The optimization finds divertors that perform the same as the parameter scan, but with a 75\% reduction in computational cost. The resulting divertors satisfy heat load requirements across varying cross-field heat diffusivities. Optimization over various islands in the equilibrium shows that it is easiest to find divertors that satisfy heat flux requirements for low-elongation islands. This algorithm presents a simple parameterization for island divertors and facilitates further physics and optimization studies.
item.dc:creator: Avigdor Veksler, Aaron Bader, Heinke Frerichs, Elizabeth Paul

item.title: High-throughput full-f gyrokinetics of the tokamak boundary
item.description: arXiv:2605.01117v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Full-f gyrokinetics of the tokamak boundary have so far been limited to individual, expert-curated cases. We report hundreds of concurrent and unsupervised simulations of the edge and scrape-off layer (SOL) in a geometry based on the Tokamak \`a Configuration Variable (TCV), scanning triangularity, elongation and heating power, each evolving turbulence for more than a millisecond, i.e. about two energy confinement times. Without tuned transport coefficients or experimental inputs, the ensemble reproduces the range of SOL heat-flux decay lengths measured in TCV, as well as the reduced SOL density fluctuations and the improved confinement of negative triangularity. The effect of triangularity on confinement is power dependent. At high power, negative triangularity improves the ion energy confinement by weakening the dominant microinstability rather than by a stronger sheared flow. At low power, positive triangularity flattens the ion temperature profile across the separatrix, which we attribute to a longer distance between the trapped ions and the cold recycling source. Local linear gyrokinetic calculations and the transport coefficients extracted from the turbulent fluxes consistently indicate a trapped-electron-mode regime, in which the conductive heat flux at the separatrix is carried by the electrons and the ion energy transport is convective. This article details the simulation setup, the ensemble statistics and the verification of the results, which are also summarized in a companion Letter.
item.dc:creator: A. C. D. Hoffmann, M. Francisquez, T. N. Bernard, G. W. Hammett

item.title: On the Shafranov shift in stellarators
item.description: arXiv:2605.22105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As first shown by Shafranov, toroidal plasmas in magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium tend to expand in major radius when the pressure is increased. Here, an average measure of the resulting Shafranov shift is introduced, and its properties are discussed for various classes of stellarator configurations. It is shown to be particularly small in quasi-helical and quasi-isodynamic stellarators with a large number of field periods, which are thus relatively robust to variations in the plasma pressure.
item.dc:creator: Per Helander, Nikita Nikulsin

item.title: Wave instabilities in anisotropic regularized Kappa plasmas: New plasma dispersion functions and numerical validation
item.description: arXiv:2606.08331v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Plasmas in space and astrophysical environments are frequently found in (quasi-)stationary states not in thermal equilibrium, indicated by velocity distribution functions (VDFs) featuring nonthermal characteristics, such as Lorentzian high-energy tails and kinetic (temperature and strahl/beam) anisotropies. For decades, in-situ observations of electrons and ions in the solar corona, solar wind or planetary magnetospheres have been modelled using so-called Kappa VDFs, whose standard form, however - depending on the considered VDF moment - imposes stringent constraints on the minimum value of the Kappa power-law parameter. Such limitations have posed difficulties on the derivation of a fully-consistent hydrodynamic formulation of suprathermal plasmas. To improve this situation, the recently proposed regularized Kappa VDF avoids strict constraints on the Kappa parameter by introducing an exponential, regularizing cut-off. In this work we assume that the plasma particles are described by regularized-Kappa VDFs that feature anisotropies not only in their thermal velocity spread parameters but also in their exponential cut-offs. The dielectric tensor components for waves propagating along a magnetic field are derived, in terms of new plasma dispersion functions. The resulting dispersion equations are solved with two complementary techniques, namely by using the analytical expressions derived here and by employing the ALPS code. This is done for physical parameters that give rise to electromagnetic and electrostatic instabilities. Both approaches show excellent agreement and the results demonstrate how an anisotropy in the regularizing cut-off of VDFs can serve, depending on an instability's nature, either as a stabilization factor or as an additional free energy source.
item.dc:creator: Rudi Gaelzer, Dustin L. Schr\"oder, Marian Lazar, Horst Fichtner

item.title: The fixed boundary plasma equilibrium basis for a one Gigawatt electric stellarator power plant
item.description: arXiv:2607.09346v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A fixed boundary stellarator equilibrium capable of producing 3 GW of fusion power (1 GW-electric) is presented as the design basis for the GIGA fusion power plant being developed by Gauss Fusion GmbH. The stellarator concept provides a steady-state, transient free, low recirculating power approach to a fusion power plant, which builds on 50 years of progress in plasma physics. A set of requirements for a fixed boundary equilibrium were determined through application of 0.5 D modeling. Optimization of a modified Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) equilibrium was performed to achieve these requirements including alpha power confinement greater than $85\%$, neoclassical effective ripple below 0.01, bootstrap current below 50 kA, and reduced turbulent heat fluxes. In order to fix the plasma volume of $1500~m^3$ during optimization, the VMEC code was modified to renormalize the boundary coefficient to the desired plasma volume. The STELLOPT stellarator optimization code was modified as well to include new bootstrap current targets, a new target for the radial electric field, and the capability to hold the magnetic field on axis at a fixed value. An intermediary conceptual design plasma and final evolved fixed boundary equilibria are compared to the original modified W7-X equilibrium. The final evolved equilibrium is shown to achieve all the necessary requirements for the GIGA fusion power plant through more detailed modeling of stability, fast ion confinement, and transport.
item.dc:creator: Samuel A. Lazerson, Ant\'onio J. Coelho, Dana Douqa, Adrian Asmund Fessler, Luisa H\"ubner, Matteo Moscheni, Eoin Hodge, Richard Kembleton, Joona Sissonen, Konsta S\"arkim\"aki, Antti Snicker, the Gauss Fusion Team

item.title: Polarized quantum effects in countable signals from intense laser - electron beam interactions
item.description: arXiv:2609.01494v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the feasibility of precision counting experiments based on laser-electron beam interactions to verify strong-field quantum electrodynamic effects, with particular emphasis on the stochastic nature of photon emission, photon polarization, and spin asymmetry. A precise Monte-Carlo model is developed using photon packets with multi-dimensional phase-space weighting, hierarchical-mesh cumulative distribution functions, and a variable time-step method. This model quantitatively reproduces the highest edge of the photon energy spectrum and the positron yield in the previous SLAC E-144 experiment. The quantized radiation back-reaction determines the highest edge tail and thus the positron yield for higher laser intensities. The spin asymmetry in photon emission and spin flip determines photon polarization in the high-energy tail, while that in pair production can be observed through the large-angle positron scattering. Our simulations predict that these effects depend on the combination of the electron-beam energy and the laser intensity, and that they could be verified in future ELI-NP experiments using sub-GeV electron beams and optical lasers with intensities ~10^22W/cm2.
item.dc:creator: Toseo Moritaka, Kensuke Homma, Kazunori Itakura

item.title: In-situ Generation of Polarized Attosecond Positron Bunches via Radiation-Wakefield Induced Two-Photon Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2609.33285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-energy, dense, spin-polarized positron beams with attosecond duration are highly desirable for advanced accelerator physics, laboratory astrophysics, and ultrafast matter-antimatter studies, yet remain beyond the capability of conventional source and injection-based plasma-acceleration schemes. We propose an integrated in-situ method for production, trapping, and accelerating polarized attosecond positron bunches in a single plasma stage. An ultraintense hollow laser propagating in a plasma channel drives a radiative wakefield, where longitudinally injected electrons emit a dense MeV gamma-ray bath through nonlinear Compton scattering. Subsequent photon-photon collisions induce linear Breit-Wheeler pair production, while linear and nonlinear radiative processes mediate polarization transfer to the produced positrons. Spin-resolved QED particle-in-cell simulations indicate that the laser-modulated wakefield naturally captures positrons born in the frontier bubble wake, forming collimated bunch trains with hundred-attosecond duration, GeV-level energies, and densities up to 10^17 cm^-3. Parameter scans demonstrate robustness against variations of laser intensity and plasma-channel density. This single-shot, source-free approach simultaneously addresses positron production, polarization, temporal compression, and plasma injection, offering a compact route toward polarized attosecond antimatter beams.
item.dc:creator: Zhen-Ke Dou, Qian Zhao, Hao-Tian Wang, Feng Wan, Jian-Xing Li

item.title: Existence and Smoothing for a Nondivergence-Form Degenerate Diffusion from Plasma-Wave Theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.13922v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove existence, positive-time smoothing, and physical admissibility of weak solutions to the degenerate parabolic Cauchy-Dirichlet problem $\partial_t u = \rho_\lambda(x) u \partial_x^2 u + \rho_\lambda(x) g(x) u$ on the half-line, where $\rho_\lambda$ vanishes at the boundary and grows at infinity. This scalar problem arises by formally reducing the system of equations given by the quasilinear theory of plasma waves in the one-dimensional case. This theory models a background distribution of electrons $f$ coupled to a spectral energy density $W$ through wave-particle resonance. For the scalar problem we construct weak solutions from weighted $L^p$ initial data and bounded reaction, admitting the unbounded, discontinuous data that the physical model demands, and lying beyond the reach of the continuous-data theories developed for nearby problems. We identify a parabolic smoothing effect for the constructed solution, namely one-sided bounds on $\partial_t u$: from merely integrable data, the solution becomes locally H\"older in space and time and locally Lipschitz in space at positive times. This spatial regularity is shown to be sharp by explicit examples. Finally, we address the quasilinear system itself, whose well-posedness remains open: we prove that the scalar solution induces a particle-wave pair $(f^{\ast}, W^{\ast})$ which is a weak solution of the system. Under nonnegativity and finite-moment hypotheses on the initial data, both components remain nonnegative and the initial mass is conserved. Moreover, the pair inherits positive-time regularity, with $W^{\ast}$ decaying quantitatively at large wavenumber and $f^{\ast}$ smoothing to a locally bounded function even when initially a measure.

item.title: Nonlocal Evolution of Magnetic Helicity across the Magnetohydrodynamic-Kinetic Interface
item.description: arXiv:2507.13213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Magnetic helicity is typically indistinguishable from noise in the solar wind inertial range. Using Parker Solar Probe measurements (0.1-0.8 au), we report a robust bihelical structure emerging at the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD)-kinetic interface. This structure, formed by a striking pair of positive and negative peaks, exhibits a systematic spectral migration toward lower frequencies with increasing heliocentric distance. Crucially, this evolution deviates from local kinetic scaling laws, such as the radial decline of the ion cyclotron frequency, reflecting a nonlocal evolution of magnetic topology. Our findings provide a new observational constraint on both nonlocal MHD transport processes and the nature of the helicity barrier in the kinetic regime.
item.dc:creator: Masatomi Iizawa, Yasuhito Narita, Tommaso Alberti, Stuart D. Bale, Axel Brandenburg, Abraham C. -L. Chian, Horia Comi\c{s}el, Shuichi Matsukiyo, Nobumitsu Yokoi

item.title: Generalized Beth--Uhlenbeck entropy formula from the $\Phi-$derivable approach
item.description: arXiv:2512.03876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive a generalized Beth-Uhlenbeck formula for the entropy of a dense fermion system with strong two-particle correlations, including scattering states and bound states. We work within the $\Phi-$derivable approach to the thermodynamic potential. The formula takes the form of an energy-momentum integral over a statistical distribution function times a unique spectral density. In the near mass-shell limit, the spectral density reduces, contrary to na\"{i}ve expectations, not to a Lorentzian but rather to a "squared Lorentzian" shape. The relation of the Beth-Uhlenbeck formula to the $\Phi$-derivable approach is exact at the two-loop level for $\Phi$. The formalism we develop, which extends the Beth-Uhlenbeck approach beyond the low-density limit, includes Mott dissociation of bound states, in accordance with Levinson's theorem, and the self-consistent back reaction of correlations in the fermion propagation. We discuss applications to further systems, such as quark matter and nuclear matter.
item.dc:creator: David Blaschke, Gerd R\"opke, Gordon Baym

item.title: Collisionless and collisional kinetics of a plasma atmosphere with spatially and temporally intermittent heating at its base
item.description: arXiv:2607.08410v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The solar corona exhibits a pronounced temperature inversion, with plasma temperatures increasing by nearly two orders of magnitude from the chromosphere to the corona. We investigate how spatially sparse and temporally intermittent stochastic heating at the base of the transition region shapes the temperature and density structure of coronal loops within a kinetic framework. Stochastic thermal boundary conditions and surface coarse graining are introduced. Analytical solutions are derived in the collisionless limit for heating-event time scales shorter or longer than the particle crossing time, and Coulomb collisions are incorporated through a reduced kinetic model describing the thermalization of suprathermal particles. In the short-time-scale regime, spatial filling factor and temporal intermittency combine into a single effective parameter controlling the suprathermal population, producing a transition region and a hot corona both within individual loops and after coarse graining. Collisions preserve this thermal structure while reducing the coronal density through progressive thermalization. In the long-time-scale regime, individual loops are nearly isothermal and the temperature inversion emerges only after coarse graining, depending solely on the spatial filling factor. Here, Coulomb collisions and optically thin radiative losses have only minor effects, while density and temperature profiles remain broadly consistent with coronal observations. These results show that sparse, intermittent heating naturally generates suprathermal particle distributions and reproduces the observed thermal structure of the solar corona within a kinetic framework, highlighting the different sensitivity of the two regimes to collisional effects.
